mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares a thermodynamic system with its surroundings?

options.A: The system includes everything in the universe, while the surroundings contain nothing.
options.B: The system is the part of the universe selected for study, and the surroundings are everything else.
options.C: The system consists only of the solid phase of a mixture, whereas the surroundings are the liquid and gas phases.
options.D: The terms system and surroundings are interchangeable and refer to the same region.

mcqs.answer: The system is the part of the universe selected for study, and the surroundings are everything else.
mcqs.explanation: In thermodynamics, a system is the specific portion of the universe that we choose to analyze. Everything outside this portion is called the surroundings. Option B captures this definition accurately; the other options misrepresent the relationship.

mcqs.question: In the context of thermodynamics, the surroundings are best described as:

options.A: The part of the universe that is being investigated.
options.B: The region that exchanges matter but not energy with the system.
options.C: Everything external to the system that can exchange energy with it.
options.D: An isolated container that prevents any exchange of matter or energy.

mcqs.answer: Everything external to the system that can exchange energy with it.
mcqs.explanation: Surroundings comprise all that lies outside the chosen system and can interact with it, primarily by exchanging energy (heat or work). Option C states this correctly. Option A describes the system, B is incorrect because surroundings can exchange both matter and energy, and D describes an isolated system, not surroundings.

mcqs.learning_point: Distinguish open, closed and isolated systems
mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly identifies an open, a closed, and an isolated system respectively?

options.A: Open – a sealed flask; Closed – a boiling kettle with lid; Isolated – a thermos flask with perfect insulation.
options.B: Open – a boiling kettle with lid; Closed – a sealed flask; Isolated – a thermos flask with perfect insulation.
options.C: Open – a thermos flask; Closed – a boiling kettle with lid; Isolated – a sealed flask.
options.D: Open – a sealed flask; Closed – a thermos flask; Isolated – a boiling kettle with lid.

mcqs.answer: Open – a boiling kettle with lid; Closed – a sealed flask; Isolated – a thermos flask with perfect insulation.
mcqs.explanation: An open system (boiling kettle with lid) can exchange both matter and energy with surroundings. A closed system (sealed flask) can exchange energy but not matter. An isolated system (thermos with perfect insulation) exchanges neither matter nor energy. Option B lists these correctly; the other options mix up the classifications.

mcqs.question: Which type of boundary allows both matter and energy to cross between the system and its surroundings?
mcqs.explanation: A permeable boundary permits the transfer of both matter and energy (heat or work). A diathermal wall allows only energy transfer, while impermeable and adiabatic walls restrict matter and/or energy. Hence, option D is correct.

mcqs.question: Select the correct definition of a thermodynamic system.

options.A: The portion of the universe selected for study, while everything else is the surroundings.
options.B: The entire universe including all its parts.
options.C: Only the solid phase of a reaction mixture.
options.D: The container that holds the reaction mixture.

mcqs.answer: The portion of the universe selected for study, while everything else is the surroundings.
mcqs.explanation: A thermodynamic system is defined as the specific part of the universe we focus on; the rest is termed the surroundings. Options B, C, and D either describe the whole universe or only parts of the system, which are inaccurate.

mcqs.question: In a chemical reaction carried out in an open beaker placed on a lab bench, which of the following best describes the surroundings?

options.C: The air, bench, and everything outside the beaker that can exchange heat with it.
options.D: The products formed in the reaction.

mcqs.answer: The air, bench, and everything outside the beaker that can exchange heat with it.
mcqs.explanation: Surroundings consist of everything external to the system (the reacting mixture in the beaker) that can interact with it, primarily by heat exchange. Option C captures this; the other options refer to parts of the system or the container itself.

mcqs.learning_point: Distinguish open, closed and isolated systems
mcqs.question: A sealed, rigid container holding a gas that does not exchange heat or matter with the outside world is an example of which type of system?
mcqs.explanation: Because the container is sealed (no matter exchange) and rigid with perfect insulation (no heat exchange), it qualifies as an isolated system. An open system would allow matter exchange, and a closed system would allow energy exchange, so options A and B are incorrect. Option D is not a standard thermodynamic classification.

mcqs.question: A beaker containing water is placed on a hot plate, and the beaker is open to the atmosphere. Which boundary type best describes the interface between the water and the surrounding air?
mcqs.explanation: The water‑air interface allows both heat transfer (energy) and the passage of water vapor (matter), characteristic of a permeable boundary. A diathermal wall would permit only energy transfer, while impermeable and adiabatic walls restrict matter and/or energy, making options A, B, and D incorrect.
